correctness.rationale: Products in the cube-zero maximal ideal factor through the symmetric form on m/m²; the one-dimensional target and nondegenerate quotient give an exact adjacency model. Perpendicularity on the projective line has fixed isotropic points and two-cycles, yielding the rank-one and rank-two decompositions. Explicit five vectors have exactly the C5 zero/nonzero pairings in every higher-rank nonalternating case, and a separate symplectic five-vector construction covers alternating characteristic-two rank >=4. Nonalternating rank >=3 contains an orthogonal nonisotropic triple via standard bilinear-form splitting. Finite checker verify.py passed all thirteen enumerated configurations; unbounded cases follow from the proof, not enumeration.

Restricting it to the alternating case overlaps the analogous extraspecial-group claim; the remaining cases require an independent orthogonal-three-vector construction and projective-line analysis, and no inspected source gives those conclusions as a corollary of a stated stronger theorem. The zero-product scalar-form theorem studies a different invariant and likewise does not imply the dichotomy.

originality.rationale: Targeted primary-literature and mathematical-index comparisons found no statement giving the sharp rank-one/rank-two versus higher-rank perfectness dichotomy for finite short local rings with one-dimensional square ideal. The 2026 bilinear construction implies the general model and may cover the alternating subcase; the published extraspecial-group commuting theorem analogously covers the symplectic obstruction, but neither covers the odd-characteristic or nonalternating characteristic-two forms together with the exact rank-two graph decomposition and arbitrary radical. The strongest accessible covering risk is an older equivalent orthogonality-graph theorem; this remains a residual uncertainty, not a claim of absolute novelty. Across accessible own historical findings, the closest 2026 claim classifies zero-divisor graph degree multisets in graded Gorenstein local rings; it neither claims the perfectness dichotomy nor implies the new induced-cycle theorem without extra arguments.

value.rationale: This is a sharp structural perfectness criterion for all finite commutative short local rings whose square ideal has residue-field dimension one. The rank-two end gives an exact complete-graph/biclique decomposition with coloring formulas; at rank three an explicit induced pentagon appears and the minimum ring size in the family is 32. It identifies the precise algebraic parameter governing departure from perfect zero-divisor graphs, bridging known principal-ideal threshold graphs and unrestricted local graph universality.
